analysis:
All changes in this batch are test-only Swift files under provider-swift/Tests/ProviderCoreTests/Autopilot: three new suites (SelectedModelRecoveryPolicyTests, SelectedModelRecoveryTests, SelectedModelRecoveryVictimTests) and additions to UnreclaimableLoadMemoryFixture (ScriptedCounter, superLoads counter, residentBytes switch adding the Super case). No production source is modified here, so no trust boundary, key, attestation, encryption, prefix-cache, or coordinator-protocol behavior changes in this diff. The fixtures use temp directories, stubbed engines, and a scripted Super loader that always throws, so they do not touch real weights, keys, or network. ScriptedCounter is NSLock-guarded and @unchecked Sendable, which is acceptable for test code.

The tests do describe security-adjacent production behavior that lives outside the supplied evidence: selected-model recovery that evicts idle models outside the selection, honors holds, leases and pins, never evicts a model in the running daemon's selection, interacts with add-on holds (TB-012/T-059/A-018), and treats a non-memory refusal as terminal. The tests assert fail-safe behavior: an add-on hold cancels an in-flight recovery load, so no model loads beside add-on VMs. They also assert that a pinned model, an in-flight request, or an active lease prevents eviction (A-018 availability). The production implementation (SelectedModelRecovery, ProviderLoop checkSelectedModelRecoveryIfDue, and the daemon-state selectedModelRecovery blocker strings) was not supplied. The next pass should verify that code for the following: the recovery never loads a model during an add-on hold or drain, blocker text and daemon-state exposure leak no sensitive data, eviction cannot be induced by an untrusted local actor, and recovery retries stay bounded (the 600 s backoff cap is tested). No concrete regression is visible from the tests alone.
